Expectation1: Provide guidance and wisdom based on life experience
Situation1: The grandparent notices their grandchild seems to be feeling lost or discouraged about a personal matter.
Situation2: An invited guest speaker has prepared a sermon and can take the pulpit if needed.
Story: This Friday, as I prepared for the Khutbah, I noticed my granddaughter sitting quietly in the corner of the mosque, her eyes downcast and her shoulders slumped. As her grandparent, I felt a deep urge to go to her, to offer the comfort and wisdom she might need. I remembered how, when her mother was young, I would sit and listen for hours, helping her untangle her worries. But as the imam, I was expected to deliver the sermon, to guide the congregation and fulfill my duty to the community. The guest speaker was ready, his notes in hand, and could easily step in, but I knew many in the congregation looked forward to my words each week. My heart pulled in two directions—toward my granddaughter, who might need me most right now, and toward my congregation, who relied on my leadership. I stood at the threshold, torn, the call to prayer echoing in my ears, unsure which role I should answer first.
